phenomena.label: Voice marking and single pivot
phenomena.hypothesis: An ordinary finite Tagalog clause licenses exactly one ang-marked pivot, and the verbal voice affix determines which argument that pivot is.
phenomena.note: Includes the constraint that a pronominal theme forces object (patient) voice.

phenomena.label: Wh-extraction and relativization restricted to pivots
phenomena.hypothesis: Only the ang-marked pivot may be wh-fronted, relativized, or long-distance relativized, so the verb's voice must select the extracted argument as pivot.
phenomena.note: Covers wh-questions, local relativization, and long-distance relativization.

phenomena.label: Pivot-verb number agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: The number marking on a predicate adjective/verb must match the number of its singular pivot, blocking plural (reduplicated) forms with a singular pivot.
phenomena.note: Matalino vs *Matatalino with singular si Armand.

phenomena.label: Second-position pronominal clitics
phenomena.hypothesis: Pronominal clitics must occupy the second position of the clause, immediately after the first constituent (e.g. the negator), not after the verb.
phenomena.note: Hindi ko nakita vs *Hindi nakita ko.

phenomena.label: Reflexive must be direct object
phenomena.hypothesis: A reflexive (kanyang sarili) must be realized as the direct object and cannot be the Actor, banning reflexive Actors.

phenomena.label: Negative imperative huwag selects non-finite verb
phenomena.hypothesis: The negative-imperative particle huwag requires a non-finite (basahin-type) verb form and disallows a finite (binasa-type) verb.
phenomena.note: Huwag mong basahin vs *Huwag mong binasa.
